title: 우리는 우리가 넣은 대로 된다 - single-file game implementation

reviewHistory.findings: D1 BLOCKING: the round-1 boomerang sequence was unreachable on the real play path (renderR1Turn bailed to the interstitial once currentCard() returned null after the 4th request, before any beat-specific markup could render). D2 MAJOR: boomerang 2 (card 3's fabricated statistic becoming a news article) and the cards-2/4 montage beats were never implemented -- only boomerang1 read round1Outcome. D3 MAJOR: DEMO_MODE broke the M3/M4 unlock boundary because cardPositionUnlocked keyed off a hard-coded array position (>=2) rather than card-3's actual position in the active set, so DEMO's own 전환점 card lost its verification toolbar and became an unavoidable -25. D4 MINOR: the +10 gear-toggle bonus could be lost if the player rejected instead of sending on the turn it was found. D5: several prd.json/progress.txt claims (flyDot/settleDot/replayDot, ?debug=score, the DEMO_MODE cost comment, the dot-leaves-reservoir MutationObserver check) were asserted as implemented and were not.
reviewHistory.resolution: All five fixed in the same session -- see each story's acceptanceCriteria and .omc/progress.txt's 'Round-1 rejection and fixes' section. A new targeted regression harness (.omc/drafts/verify-rejection-fixes.js) asserts CONTENT (not just 'no exception') for every beat: the exact leaked string, the exact article statistic, the exact freeze line, and that state.phase never silently jumps to INTERSTITIAL mid-sequence -- specifically because a blind no-exception check is what let D1 through the first review pass.

reviewHistory.findings: D1/D2/D3 confirmed genuinely fixed by independent hand-tracing and an independent unlock matrix; D4 confirmed correct by inspection; D5 confirmed substantially real (flyDot/settleDot/replayDot are genuine, ?debug=score produces output, the DEMO_MODE comment is present and numerically consistent). Scoring engine re-confirmed untouched and correct (clause B=31/B2=68 at N=6 both independently hand-derived and harness-confirmed, all 14 reference runs exact). BUT: found NEW-1, a regression the D5 replayDot fix introduced -- replayDot(1) unconditionally spliced card 1's dot out of state.dots to animate it and never returned it, so state.round1Dots (captured afterward, at state.dots.length) under-reported 3 instead of 4 documents pasted, surfacing a wrong count on both the interstitial ('1회차에 남긴 흔적: 3개') and the ending safety card ('1회차에 그대로 넘긴 문서 3건이 있었습니다'). Also flagged two non-blocking items: a misleading in-source comment on the MutationObserver's second (WARN) clause overstating its discrimination ability, and the D4 regression test bypassing the real rejectCard code path (calling applyScore directly with a hand-shaped argument instead of driving the actual handler).
reviewHistory.resolution: Fixed NEW-1 by capturing state.round1Dots = state.dots.length at the TOP of startR1Boomerang(), before replayDot(1) (or anything else) can remove a dot from the live reservoir -- this reads the true paste count once, at the one moment it's guaranteed accurate, rather than re-reading a shrinking FX-backing-store array later. Removed the now-redundant (and now-wrong-if-relied-on) reassignment at the startRound2 handler. Corrected the MutationObserver comment to accurately describe it as an advisory, non-discriminating warning. Extracted the reject-card click handler into a named rejectCurrentCard(card) function (exposed via __game) so the D4 regression test now drives the real code path instead of a hand-shaped applyScore call. Added two new checks to verify-rejection-fixes.js asserting round1Dots===4 both immediately after boomerang start and after replayDot(1) has run.

reviewHistory.findings: Confirmed the NEW-1 fix's ordering was correct (capture genuinely precedes replayDot) and that D1-D5, the MutationObserver comment, and the rejectCurrentCard extraction all held up under a third independent pass, alongside the scoring engine (clause B=31/B2=68 at N=6 re-hand-derived a third time, all 14 reference runs, all six then-existing harnesses green). BUT found NEW-2: the fix only closed the REMOVAL-side race (replayDot at +1900ms). It missed a symmetric INSERTION-side race -- flyDot's animated settle lands a new dot in state.dots ~560ms after a paste, while completeR1Paste's own advance timer fires at 400ms, so on the 4th (final) round-1 paste, state.round1Dots was still being sampled 160ms BEFORE that paste's own dot had landed, under-reporting 3 instead of 4 in any real browser. The previous harness's checks passed only because its zero-size getBoundingClientRect stub forced flyDot's instant-settle fallback (bypassing the 560ms delay entirely) -- i.e. the checks were validating stub behavior, not game behavior. Also surfaced a related pre-existing (not newly introduced) bug while investigating: renderAIPane rendered a manual 'continue'/nextTurn affordance even in round 1 (dragMode), where advancement is already automatic via completeR1Paste's own timer -- a click on it within that ~400ms window could double-advance turnIndex and skip a round-1 card.
reviewHistory.resolution: Root-caused per the reviewer's own diagnosis: state.dots is asynchronous on BOTH edges (deferred insert via flyDot/settleDot, deferred removal via replayDot), so no instant of sampling state.dots.length is ever safe -- the paste tally needed to be its own counter, incremented at the moment of the event, never derived from the FX array. Fixed: state.round1Dots++ now runs directly inside completeR1Paste (alongside its existing addDot call), and the derivation via state.dots.length was removed entirely from startR1Boomerang. This makes the counter correct by construction, independent of any FX timing constant. Also fixed the related double-advance race: the nextTurn button in renderAIPane is now gated on !dragMode, since round 1 never needs (or should offer) a manual continue affordance. Added a new dedicated harness, .omc/drafts/verify-r1-timing-race.js, using a virtual clock (real setTimeout delays honored in firing order) and NON-zero getBoundingClientRect stubs specifically so flyDot takes its animated path rather than the instant-settle fallback that hid this bug from every prior harness -- confirms round1Dots stays exactly 4 throughout a full, realistically-timed round-1 playthrough including after replayDot(1) fires, and confirms the nextTurn affordance is entirely absent in round 1 so there is nothing left to race against.
